project: Automatos AI — PRD-251 Socials, Wave 1: the video engine
description: Wave 1 of PRD-251 (docs/PRDS/PRD-251-SOCIALS.md, D1-D17 binding, the owner's Wave 1 answers of 2026-09-23 in its status block). Wave 0 lands on main through PR #783 (test/customer-night → main; #782 closes as landed there). Launched after that, this wave is cut from main and its migration chains onto f049_prd251_merge_heads; launched before, it stacks on feat/prd-251-socials. Diff base for every check: `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd251w1.sh --print-base`. Twenty stories. US-101..US-114, the engine: the media-render service (container + CI job, API, orchestrator client with the render lifecycle, quotas Basic 10 / Pro 60 / Business 240 minutes, compose profile `media`, Railway manifest at 4 vCPU / 8 GB with two renders at once), the media cost lane (S4.4, moved into this wave), templates as data with the four reference templates and the image families, the brand kit, facts with sources, the media capability registry, voice, music, the infographic, and footage from the workspace's Composio toolkits. S1.9 (the 'social video director' skill) is NOT in this loop: the owner's rule is that skills are authored in the automatos-skills repo first, then synced into this repo's seed, and this loop never edits automatos-skills or a generated seed. Nothing here schedules, publishes or adds the full composer — Waves 2 and 3. US-115..US-120, the agent layer (owner, 2026-09-23: reuse what exists; pulled forward from Waves 3-4): brand-kit tools, Socials draft tools (S4.1), social formats in generate_document and a general image tool, the S3.5 post gate, built-in skills synced from automatos-skills, and the Socials marketplace package (two agents, four playbooks, guided setup).

userStories.title: S1.1b — The media-render API: check, render, voice, mix, concurrency
userStories.description: The service's HTTP API (aiohttp, like the worker). POST /render takes a composition bundle: the template's html/css, the variables, brand assets inlined as data: URIs (logo, font files), media inputs as presigned GET URLs to OUR storage only (the service refuses any other host — allowlist from config, never arbitrary URLs), and an audio plan (voice lines, music track id and window, SFX cues). It runs `hyperframes check` first and refuses with 422 carrying the lint/layout/contrast findings; otherwise renders (--quality delivery --fps 30) and returns a job id. GET /render/{id} reports status, the check report and timings; GET /render/{id}/output/{name} streams the file. POST /tts synthesises Kokoro lines (one WAV per line, returns durations; voice and speed parameters, default af_heart at 0.95). The mix is ffmpeg exactly as the reference: voice placed with adelay, music ducked by sidechaincompress (threshold 0.015, ratio 10, attack 10, release 420) at x0.6, SFX, loudnorm I=-14 TP=-1.5 LRA=11. Concurrency (owner, 2026-09-23): at most TWO renders at once overall and ONE per workspace; further jobs queue FIFO. Every limit and timeout is config.
acceptanceCriteria: In the CI job: rendering the fixture bundle through POST /render returns an MP4 whose integrated loudness is -14 ± 1 LUFS (ebur128 in the job log).
A bundle with a lint error returns 422 with the findings and renders nothing (test).
A media URL outside the storage allowlist is refused before any fetch (test).
Three submissions from two workspaces: two run, the third queues; two from the SAME workspace never run at once (test with a stub renderer).
Missing or wrong X-Internal-Token gets 401; /health is open (test).

userStories.notes: The reference mix: docs/PRDS/prd251-reference/mix-reference.py; voice: synth-vo-reference.py. Word timing (energy gaps: 10 ms hops, 4% threshold, gaps >= 70 ms) is how text lands on words — expose it from /tts. The renderer assembles; it never calls a generation provider (D3).
